title: Normalization: store each fact once

kcs.statement: Normalization stores each fact in exactly one row, so an update touches one place and copies cannot disagree (no update anomaly).
A normalized schema answers reads that combine entities with joins, which grow expensive as tables grow and are hard to run when tables live on different machines.

problem_ideas: An orders table repeats the customer's address on every row; show the update anomaly when the customer moves
Split a flat spreadsheet of (student, course, instructor, instructor_email) into normalized tables
Count the joins needed to render a news-feed item (post, author, like count, top comment) in a fully normalized schema
Spot the anomaly in a schema where product price is stored on both products and cart_items
Explain why a normalized schema is the safe default for a payments ledger
Given three queries, say which become slow first as tables grow to a billion rows
